Cellular shades and insulation

Cellular shades, also called honeycomb shades, trap air within fabric pockets. They are an option to compare when comfort near a window is a concern. Compare the cell construction, light control, and fit. Energy savings depend on the windows, installation, and how you use the shades.

Solar shades for exposed windows

Solar screen fabrics can reduce glare while allowing an outward view during daylight. Different openness levels change the balance of view and screening. Ask to compare samples where the sun is strongest, and plan a separate privacy solution if the mesh does not meet your needs at night.

Wood and faux wood blinds

Real wood offers natural grain and a choice of finishes. Faux wood is an alternative to discuss where moisture resistance and cleaning matter, including kitchens and bathrooms. We can show you how the materials differ in weight, finish, and care so you can choose what suits the room.

Controls for high or hard-to-reach windows

Fit the treatment to the opening

A custom order starts with the window details. We check the frame and how you need to use the space before recommending a mounting approach.

Keep existing details visible

Older trim and unusual openings may need a different mount from a deep, square recess. We check handles, frame depth, and the glass you want to keep exposed. Shutter frame and panel choices should also allow the window to operate as intended.

Balance privacy and open views

For wide glass or a view across your property, consider what will remain visible when the treatment is raised, tilted, or drawn. Talk through both daytime glare and nighttime privacy. Facing open space does not remove the need to check sightlines after dark.

Plan larger and newer rooms

Several adjacent windows may need coordinated fabric and control choices, even when the openings differ. Share any construction work still underway and your target schedule. We confirm final measurements and product availability before the order goes ahead.

Custom Window Treatments for Leo-Cedarville Homes

Cellular Shades for Energy Efficiency

Rural Indiana properties often face higher heating and cooling costs due to larger square footage and more exposure to the elements. Cellular shades, also called honeycomb shades, create insulating barriers that keep your Leo-Cedarville home comfortable year-round. The unique honeycomb structure traps air, reducing heat transfer through your windows.

Many Leo-Cedarville homeowners have larger windows to capture views of their property, which means more potential for energy loss. We've installed cellular shades throughout the area, and residents consistently report improved comfort and lower utility bills. Double-cell options provide maximum insulation for those particularly drafty rooms or north-facing windows that never seem to warm up.

Motorized Blinds and Shades

Leo-Cedarville homes often feature high ceilings, large great rooms, and windows that would require a ladder to reach. Motorized window treatments solve this challenge elegantly. Control your blinds and shades from your phone, a wall switch, or voice commands through your smart home system.

Beyond convenience, motorization offers significant safety benefits for families with young children by eliminating cords entirely. You can also program your shades to open with sunrise and close at sunset, ensuring consistent energy savings without daily effort. For homeowners who travel or spend time away, scheduled operation makes your home appear occupied, a valuable security feature in rural areas.

Plantation Shutters

Plantation shutters bring timeless elegance to Leo-Cedarville homes while providing exceptional durability and insulation. Their solid construction withstands the test of time, and the adjustable louvers give you precise control over light and privacy. We've found shutters particularly popular in living rooms, dining rooms, and master bedrooms where homeowners want that refined, custom look.

Solar Shades and UV Protection

Large windows that showcase your Leo-Cedarville property's natural surroundings also expose your home to intense UV radiation. Solar shades filter harmful rays while preserving your views, you get sun protection without losing the connection to your outdoor space. This matters tremendously for furniture, flooring, and artwork that can fade from sun exposure.

Solar shades work exceptionally well in sunrooms, home offices, and any space with significant southern or western exposure. They reduce glare on screens and eliminate hot spots without darkening your rooms. Many Leo-Cedarville residents appreciate how solar shades maintain their home's bright, open feeling while providing practical protection.

Wood Blinds and Faux Wood Blinds

For homeowners who love the classic look of wood, both real wood and faux wood blinds offer attractive options. Real wood blinds bring natural warmth and beauty, perfect for formal spaces and homes with traditional décor. Faux wood blinds deliver the same aesthetic appeal with added moisture resistance and durability, making them ideal for kitchens, bathrooms, and high-humidity areas.

Leo-Cedarville's variable climate, hot summers and cold winters, means window treatments need to withstand temperature fluctuations. Faux wood blinds excel in these conditions without warping, cracking, or fading. They're also an excellent value, giving you the upscale look of real wood at a more accessible price point.
